PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 11/21/29 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Persistent cough with yellow sputum, moderate shortness of breath, and ongoing fatigue.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for a follow-up visit one week after the initiation of oral Doxycycline and continuation of oral Prednisone for his chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation. He reports a slight improvement in his cough, stating it is less frequent, though it remains productive with yellow sputum. His shortness of breath has shown minimal improvement, particularly during exertion, and he continues to experience chest tightness. Fatigue persists, affecting his daily activities, although he notes a marginal increase in his energy levels compared to the previous week. He denies any new onset of fever, chills, or hemoptysis.
Mr. Fairfax has adhered to his medication regimen, including the increased dose of Salmeterol and the addition of Tiotropium. He continues to use nebulized albuterol, though he reports needing it somewhat less frequently than before.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + ongoing fatigue, - weight loss, - fever, - chills, - night sweats. Pulmonary - + productive cough with yellow sputum, + moderate wheezing, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain, - orthopnea, - paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - no joint pain. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: - Blood Pressure: 132/78 mmHg - Heart Rate: 78 bpm - Respiratory Rate: 26 breaths/min - Oxygen Saturation: 88% on room air.
General: The patient appears fatigued but is in no acute distress.
HEENT: No nasal flaring; oropharynx clear, no signs of dehydration.
Lungs: Moderate wheezing on auscultation; decreased breath sounds bilaterally; prolonged expiration with audible rhonchi.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs or gallops; peripheral pulses intact and symmetric.
Extremities: No edema; no tenderness on palpation.
ASSESSMENT
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) with ongoing exacerbation; moderate improvement in symptoms but still insufficient response to current treatment, evidenced by persistent cough, shortness of breath, and fatigue. 2. Congestive heart failure stable; no signs of fluid overload or exacerbation. 3. Persistent fatigue likely multifactorial, with contributions from respiratory symptoms and potential deconditioning.
PLAN
1. Continue Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for an additional 5 days, as there is a slight improvement in sputum production, suggesting a bacterial component may still be present. 2. Continue oral Prednisone 20 mg daily for another week to manage inflammation associated with COPD exacerbation. 3. Maintain the current regimen of Salmeterol 50 mcg twice daily and Tiotropium 18 mcg once daily to optimize bronchodilation; consider increasing the frequency of nebulized albuterol to every 4 hours as needed for symptomatic relief. 4. Encourage Mr. Fairfax to engage in light physical activity as tolerated to combat deconditioning and improve overall stamina. 5. Schedule follow-up in one week to reassess respiratory status, sputum characteristics, and fatigue levels. If symptoms do not show significant improvement, consider referral to a pulmonary specialist for further evaluation, including pulmonary function testing.
DISPOSITION
Mr. Fairfax was discharged home with the continuation of his current medication regimen, including Doxycycline and Prednisone, and was advised on the importance of adhering to his treatment plan. He was encouraged to keep a detailed symptom diary and to monitor for any changes in his condition. A follow-up appointment has been scheduled for one week from today to evaluate the effectiveness of the ongoing treatment and to make necessary adjustments based on his clinical progress.
